entries.topic: Elections and access: electoral rules, turnout over time, disqualifications (Israel, US)

claims.text: Israel's electoral threshold: 1.0% (1951–1992), 1.5% (1992–2003), 2.0% (2004–2013), 3.25% from 2014 (applied from the 2015 election); in November 2022 almost 420,000 votes (8.8% of valid votes, about 10 seats' worth) went to lists below the threshold; the 2022 threshold was 154,854 votes; registered voters 6.789m (Nov 2022), projected 7.561m by 30 Sep 2026; turnout above 80% until the late 1960s, high 70s 1970s–1990s, mid-60s to low 70s since the second intifada

The Governance Law passed the Knesset on 18 March 2014 raised the threshold from 2% to 3.25%; INSS put Arab turnout at about 50% and 2013 overall turnout at some 56% of eligible voters [the latter conflicts with Knesset-based 63.9%]
March 2021 turnout of 67.4% was the third-lowest in Israel's history; nearly 6.78m eligible for 2022
INSS: Arab turnout 53.2% in 2022, 44.6% in March 2021, 64.8% in 2020
Census Bureau: 65.3% of voting-age citizens voted in 2024, 1.5 points below 2020 (≈66.8%) and 13.1 points above the 2022 midterm
Census Bureau (2 May 2023): 52.2% of adult citizens voted in the 2022 midterms, second-highest midterm since 2000; 2018 slightly higher

In September 2026 Israel's Central Elections Committee voted to disqualify the Joint List (Hadash, Ta'al, Balad) and Ra'am and candidates Ofer Cassif and Sami Abu Shehadeh; on 2 October 2026 the Supreme Court unanimously overturned the party bans and reinstated Cassif 7–2; Abu Shehadeh withdrew, calling it 'a historical catastrophe for democracy'; push against him attributed to Ben-Gvir; vote on 27 Oct 2026

entries.topic: Democracy indices over time: Freedom House, V-Dem, RSF, IDI Democracy Index

claims.text: Freedom House 2026 (covering 2025): US 81/100 (PR 32/40, CL 49/60), Free, down from 84; 2024 cycle most expensive at about $16bn; FEC left with two members; proof-of-citizenship EO of March 2025 permanently blocked in October; Texas, Missouri, North Carolina and California redrew maps; AP excluded over Gulf of Mexico naming; CPB defunded and closed; 188 assaults on journalists; FCC chair threatened licences; hundreds of visas revoked, some over speech on the Israel-Hamas war; September federal ruling found noncitizens unfairly targeted for speech; 'No Kings' protests ~5m in June; DOJ public integrity unit cut from 36 to two lawyers; 18 inspectors general removed; C2 anticorruption down 3→2
AFP: the US score of 81 is its lowest since the series began; down three points; cited 'legislative dysfunction and executive dominance' and pressure on free expression; equal to South Africa
Freedom House 2021: US aggregate score declined 11 points from 94 in 2010 to 83 in 2020, among the 25 largest declines

Freedom House 2026: Israel 73/100 (PR 34/40, CL 39/60), Free; scores do not reflect actions in Gaza or the West Bank, rated separately: West Bank 22, Gaza 2 (Not Free); elections A1–A3 4/4; free media 3/4; NGO freedom 2/4; assembly 3/4; B4 minority political rights 2/4; journalist Israel Frey arrested over a post; lecturer arrested over posts

Freedom House 2025 (Israel 73): 2012 law requires quarterly reporting of foreign-government support to NGOs; 2016 law requires NGOs mostly funded by foreign governments to disclose it publicly, mainly affecting left-leaning groups; 2017 law bars entry to foreigners who publicly back boycotts of Israel or settlements; 2011 Boycott Law exposes boycott advocates to civil suits; April 2024 temporary law allows withdrawing foreign outlets' licences for renewable 45-day periods, Al Jazeera shut in May 2024; Nov 2024 government halted state advertising with Haaretz; protests widely permitted, some Arab cease-fire demonstrations disallowed, police sometimes used excessive force; parties rely mostly on public funding allocated by electoral performance, private donations strictly limited; threshold 3.25% since 2015; parties denying Israel's Jewish character, opposing democracy, inciting racism or supporting terrorism can be barred, applied to far-right Jewish and Arab parties, Supreme Court overturned several disqualifications

V-Dem 2026: the US lost liberal-democracy status in 2025 for the first time in over 50 years, now electoral democracy (ED+); a new autocratizer, episode from 2023, LDI decline −0.218; legislative constraints lost about a third of their value, lowest in over 100 years; freedom of expression and media at lowest in 60 years. Israel: electoral democracy (ED+), lost liberal-democracy status in 2023, the only electoral democracy in MENA; not listed among autocratizers

RSF 2026: Israel 116th of 180 (score 46.46), from 112th (51.055) in 2025; most media owned by large corporations or magnates; far-right Channel 14 second most watched in 2023; politicians have significant influence over regulator appointments; communications minister proposed privatising or closing public radio and called for boycott of Haaretz in 2024; prior military censorship of security reporting
RSF 2026: US 64th, score 62.61, down seven places; 'US media continue to face rising political polarization'
RSF 2026 (30 Apr 2026): more than 220 Palestinian journalists killed by the Israeli army since 7 Oct 2023, at least 70 because of their work; US 64th 'slipping due to growing political pressure'

IDI Democracy Index 2025 (22 Dec 2025): 24% (May) / 27% (Nov) of Jewish and 12% of Arab respondents rate Israeli democracy good or excellent; 53% of Jews and 70% of Arabs prefer to keep political opinions quiet among strangers, rising since 2016–17; 65.5% expect the next elections to be free and fair; 46.5% agree it would be best to dismantle all political institutions and start over; trust in nearly all institutions below multi-year average

entries.topic: Speech, boycott and NGO laws; press and media ownership

claims.text: Avneri v. Knesset (15 Apr 2015), nine-justice panel: Boycott Law s.1 covers calls for economic, cultural or academic boycott of Israel, its institutions or 'an area in its control'; s.2 civil tort upheld 5–4; s.2(c) damages without proof of harm struck down unanimously; ss.3–4 denial of tenders and state benefits upheld; Melcer: such boycott calls 'do not fall under the classic purposes of free speech'

On 16 Feb 2025 the Ministerial Committee for Legislation backed Ariel Kallner's bill to tax foreign-government donations to NGOs at 80% and let courts disregard petitions by groups 'primarily financed by a foreign political entity'; exempts NGOs with Israeli state funding; finance minister may exempt; ACRI's Noa Sattath: 'a direct assault on Israel's democracy'; a 2023 version (65% tax) was shelved in May 2023 after pushback incl. the Biden administration
Media Line (5 May 2025): the bill was at committee stage and needed three readings; exempts groups under ₪100,000 revenue; Kallner: it 'will block improper foreign interference'
JPost (27 May 2025): the bill was still a proposal before the Constitution, Law and Justice Committee; no readings reported
Times of Israel (16 Feb 2025) mentions the 2017 'V15 law', aimed at stopping wealthy donors from using political organisations to bypass election-funding laws

entries.topic: Audit re-checks for Part Three (Callais ruling, Freedom House US details)

claims.text: Louisiana v. Callais decided 29 April 2026, 6-3 (Alito; Kagan dissenting with Sotomayor and Jackson): compliance with Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act did not justify Louisiana's second majority-Black district, an unconstitutional racial gerrymander; Section 2 not struck down but vote-dilution claims made much harder to win

Freedom House 2026: 2024 'final results were widely accepted'; Menendez 'sentenced to 11 years in prison in January 2025' for 'secretly working on behalf of the Egyptian and Qatari governments' in exchange for bribes; National Guard placed in Los Angeles without the governor's consent; Chicago and Portland deployments abandoned 'in late December after a series of adverse court rulings'; government 'said it would appeal' the September speech ruling
